title: How do we multiply powers of the same letter?
description: Pee to the power four times pee to the power six is written as one power by counting the pees. The same idea splits two to the power nine and five to the power seven into smaller powers that are easy to work out. Keeko's doubt is that four times six gives pee to the power twenty four.
teaching_notes: One idea: powers of the same number or letter are joined by counting all the equal factors, so the small numbers add. Watch for students who multiply the small numbers instead of adding them.

source: Write p⁴ × p to the power 6 as one power, and compute 2 to t
video_script.why: The child can write a repeated multiplication as a power and now joins two powers of the same letter and splits a big power into two smaller ones.
video_script.substitution: The book's own pee to the power four times pee to the power six, with the book's own two to the power nine and five to the power seven.
video_script.anchor: four pees and six pees written in a row on the board, then joined into one row of pees
video_script.wrong_answer: pee to the power twenty four
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks four times six gives pee to the power twenty four. Counting the pees shows there are only ten, because four pees and six pees joined make ten pees.
video_script.payoff_line: Five to the power seven is seventy eight thousand one hundred twenty five

final_answer.spoken: pee to the power ten; five hundred twelve; and seventy eight thousand one hundred twenty five

never_show: p to the power 24 marked as right
maths_rules: p⁴ × p⁶ = (p × p × p × p) × (p × p × p × p × p × p) = ten p's = p¹⁰; 4 + 6 = 10
video_script.design: One idea: count the equal factors, so the small numbers add. The row of pees stays on the board all video; the last product is left open until the answer; one slip at the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about multiplying powers of the same letter.
<bookmark mark='pee'/>Pee to the power four times pee to the power six is on the board.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How can we write it as one power?
And how can we use it for two to the power nine and five to the power seven?

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Pee to the power four means four pees multiplied.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Pee to the power six means six pees multiplied.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, pee to the power four times pee to the power six.
<bookmark mark='also'/>We also have two to the power nine and five to the power seven.

beats.on_screen: To find: p⁴ × p⁶ as one power; the values of 2⁹ and 5⁷ by splitting
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write the first as one power.
Then we work out the other two by splitting each power in two.

beats.on_screen: p⁴ × p⁶ = (p × p × p × p) × (p × p × p × p × p × p) = p¹⁰; 4 + 6 = 10

marks.one: the four p's and the six p's are joined in one row

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, four pees multiplied by six pees makes ten pees multiplied.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>That is pee to the power ten, because four and six make ten.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, split nine as four and five.
Two to the power nine is two to the power four times two to the power five.
<bookmark mark='sixteen'/>Two to the power four is sixteen, and two to the power five is thirty two.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Sixteen times thirty two is five hundred twelve.

marks.mult: 125 × 625 is written with the result left open

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, split seven as three and four.
Five to the power seven is five cubed times five to the power four.
<bookmark mark='values'/>Five cubed is one hundred twenty five, and five to the power four is six hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>One hundred twenty five times six hundred twenty five is left to find.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>Five to the power seven is seventy eight thousand one hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Pee to the power four times pee to the power six is pee to the power ten.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>Two to the power nine is five hundred twelve.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks four times six gives pee to the power twenty four.
<bookmark mark='count'/>But count the pees on the board, and there are only ten.
Four pees and six pees joined make ten pees, not twenty four.
